payload.comment:
The deterministic finding 'OOD AUROC is below random chance' is confirmed by the evidence. The selected score (max_softmax) yields test AUROCs of 0.879 (σ=0.15), 0.301 (σ=0.25), and 0.0018 (σ=0.4), giving an arithmetic mean of (0.878883+0.300678+0.001771)/3 = 0.393777, matching the reported ood_auroc. This is below 0.5, meaning the model's confidence is anti-correlated with OOD-ness at moderate-to-high corruption levels: the model is more confident on more corrupted samples than on in-distribution ones. This renders the confidence-threshold abstention mechanism counterproductive for OOD detection—at σ=0.4 the AUROC of 0.0018 indicates near-perfect inversion of the correct ranking.

The in-distribution selective prediction is functional: at 80% target coverage the test coverage is 65.3%, accuracy on covered samples rises from 92.1% to 97.6%, and selective risk is 2.43%. The risk-coverage curve is monotone and reasonable. The human review queue (2492 samples) is properly documented with SHA-256 integrity.

However, the core purpose of an abstention mechanism—flagging samples the model cannot reliably handle—fails for the OOD axis. The pipeline should either (a) adopt a complementary OOD detector (e.g., Mahalanobis distance, energy score, or ensemble disagreement) that does not rely solely on max-softmax confidence, (b) explicitly scope the abstention guarantee to in-distribution uncertainty only and document the OOD limitation in the report, or (c) adjust the corruption proxy to a regime where confidence-based detection is meaningful. As currently configured, the abstention gate provides no OOD protection and may actively misroute OOD samples into the 'covered' (auto-accepted) set at higher noise levels.

Secondary observations (non-deterministic, informational): (1) Val-test accuracy gap of ~7.5 pp (99.6% vs 92.1%) suggests moderate overfitting or distribution shift between splits; (2) Class 7 (cancer-associated stroma) recall is 56.5% (F1=0.70), the weakest class, with 110/421 misclassified primarily to smooth muscle and debris; (3) The compact_conv_stem_transformer extension remains pending_review—irrelevant to the current ResNet18 run but should be resolved before any future trial selects it; (4) Upstream architecture_research and data_audit stages carry action=revise for non-blocking process inconsistencies (augmentation gate status, null model digest, curated excerpt retrieval)—none affect the current run's correctness.

No critical deterministic findings are present. The OOD AUROC warning is the sole deterministic issue and warrants revision of the OOD detection strategy or explicit scoping of the abstention guarantee before the report is finalized.
